summary: Nepal's Department of Immigration says citizens of the countries it lists cannot obtain a visa on arrival and that all other passport holders may obtain one at Tribhuvan International Airport and other designated entry points; it lists tourist visa fees of USD 30 for 15 days, USD 50 for 30 days and USD 125 for 90 days, all multiple entry, and says Indian citizens do not require a visa. The UK government says you can apply online for a visa on arrival up to 15 days before you arrive and then collect and pay for it at the airport.

passportValidity.text: The UK FCDO says that to avoid problems at immigration your passport should have an expiry date at least 6 months after your date of entry into Nepal. The Department of Immigration asks eVisa applicants to upload a scanned passport copy valid for at least 6 months.

source.name: UK FCDO — Nepal travel advice, entry requirements

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: The UK FCDO says that to enter Nepal you must have a certificate to prove you have had a yellow fever vaccination if you are coming from a country listed as a transmission risk. WHO's country list gives the requirement for travellers aged 9 months or over arriving from countries with risk of yellow fever transmission, and for travellers who transited for more than 12 hours through an airport of such a country.

source.name: UK FCDO — Nepal travel advice, entry requirements

alsoStatedOn.name: WHO — International Travel and Health, country list: vaccination requirements and WHO recommendations (2022)

vaccinations.name: Polio
vaccinations.text: The UK FCDO says that to enter Nepal you must have a certificate to prove you have had a polio vaccine if you are coming from certain countries with a transmission risk.

source.name: UK FCDO — Nepal travel advice, entry requirements

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states whether travel insurance is required to enter Nepal. The UK FCDO says that at border control you may need to show a travel insurance document covering healthcare costs, repatriation and other emergencies in Nepal, and confirmation of where you will spend your first night. For trekking, the UK FCDO advises insurance that covers mountain rescue and helicopter costs; it says helicopter evacuation usually costs between £1,000 and £2,000 or more per flying hour.

source.name: UK FCDO — Nepal travel advice, entry requirements ("Checks at border control")

currencyLimits.text: The UK FCDO says you must declare on a customs form on arrival any amount above USD 5,000 in banknotes, or USD 10,000 in notes and travellers' cheques combined. Canada's travel advice says the use of Indian rupee notes greater than 100 INR is prohibited and that it is illegal to take Nepalese rupee banknotes out of the country.

notes: The UK FCDO says some skincare products and e-cigarette refills may contain ingredients that are illegal in Nepal, such as CBD; police who find you with them may seize them and charge you with drug possession.

The UK FCDO says it is illegal to buy, sell, kill or capture any wild animal or trade its parts without a licence, and that Nepal is a signatory to CITES, which bans trade of wildlife products without a permit.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says Nepal's economy is largely cash-based, though credit cards can be used in major stores, hotels and restaurants and ATMs are available in larger cities such as Kathmandu and Pokhara. The UK FCDO says ATMs are not reliable outside main tourist sites, and that in remote areas ATMs may not be available and credit cards may not be accepted.

safety.text: The UK FCDO says there is a low rate of serious crime in Nepal but warns of pickpockets and bag-snatchers, and says political protests and strikes are fairly common and disrupt transport. It says major flooding on 26 August 2026 caused widespread damage in Rasuwa district and the Nepal–China border area, and that the authorities have warned of the risk of further flooding.

tips.text: The UK FCDO says you need a valid permit and a TIMS (Trekking Information Management System) card to enter Nepal's main trekking regions, and that all foreign independent trekkers must use a local guide or porter in national parks and protected areas.

The UK FCDO advises making sure your insurance includes cover for mountain rescue services and helicopter costs, and warns that rapid helicopter evacuation may be difficult to get in a remote area. It also reports isolated cases of trekking guides taking inexperienced trekkers to high altitudes too quickly and then calling in expensive helicopter medivacs from which the guides take a cut.

The UK FCDO says you can apply online for a visa on arrival up to 15 days before you arrive, then collect and pay at the airport. You can pay by card, but bring cash as a back-up — US dollars are preferred.

The Department of Immigration lists an overstay fine of USD 5 per day, and the UK FCDO says overstaying is a serious crime that can lead to significant fines or imprisonment. The FCDO says you can extend your visa online to a total of 150 days in one year.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Nepal?
faq.answer: Yes. Nepal's Department of Immigration lists the countries whose citizens cannot obtain a visa on arrival — the United States is not among them — and says all other passport holders may obtain a visa on arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport and other designated entry points. It lists tourist visa fees of USD 30 for 15 days, USD 50 for 30 days and USD 125 for 90 days, all multiple entry. The UK government says you can pay by card but should have cash as a back-up, with US dollars the preferred currency.

faq.question: Do Indian citizens need a visa for Nepal?
faq.answer: No. The Department of Immigration says Indian citizens do not require a visa to enter Nepal.

faq.question: How does Nepal's visa on arrival work?
faq.answer: The UK FCDO says you can apply online up to 15 days before you arrive and then collect and pay for the visa at the airport using your submission receipt, or apply using the forms or terminals at the airport and queue. You can pay by card, but should have cash as a back-up, with US dollars preferred.

faq.question: Can I extend my Nepal tourist visa?
faq.answer: Yes. The Department of Immigration lists the extension fee as USD 3 per day with a minimum of 15 days, and says tourist visas can be extended inside Nepal up to a combined maximum of 150 days per visa year; the UK FCDO says you can extend online to a total of 150 days in one year.

faq.question: Do I need permits for trekking in Nepal besides the visa?
faq.answer: Yes. The UK FCDO says you need a valid permit and a TIMS card to enter Nepal's main trekking regions, and that all foreign independent trekkers must use a local guide or porter in national parks and protected areas. It points to the Nepal Tourism Board for the TIMS requirements.

entryRequirements.passportValidity.text: To avoid problems at immigration, make sure your passport has an ‘expiry date’ at least 6 months after your date of entry into Nepal.
Upload a scanned passport copy (valid ≥6 months)

entryRequirements.vaccinations.yellow-fe.text: To enter Nepal, you must have a certificate to prove you’ve had: a yellow fever vaccination if you’re coming from a country listed as a transmission risk

proof of vaccination against yellow fever is required for travellers aged 9 months or over arriving from countries with risk of yellow fever transmission , and for travellers having transited for more than 12 hours through an airport of a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.

entryRequirements.vaccinations.polio.text: a polio vaccine, if you’re coming from certain countries with a transmission risk

entryRequirements.travelInsurance.text: At border control, you may need to show: a travel insurance document which has cover for healthcare costs including repatriation and other emergencies while you are in Nepal confirmation of where you will spend your first night, for example, a hotel booking
Make sure your insurance includes cover for mountain rescue services and helicopter costs.
This usually costs between £1,000 and £2,000 or more per flying hour.

entryRequirements.declarations.online-vi.text: You can apply online for a visa on arrival up to 15 days in advance of your arrival. Using your submission receipt, you then collect and pay for your visa at the airport. You can also apply using the forms or terminals available at the airport

entryRequirements.customs.currencyLimits.text: You must declare on a customs form on arrival any amount above the value of 5,000 US dollars in banknotes or 10,000 dollars in notes and travellers cheques combined.
However, the use of notes greater than 100 INR is prohibited.
It is illegal to take NPR banknotes out of the country.

entryRequirements.customs.notes.0.text: Some skincare products and e-cigarette refills may contain ingredients that are illegal in Nepal such as cannabidiol (CBD). If the police find you with products containing CBD, they may seize them and charge you with drug possession.

entryRequirements.customs.notes.1.text: It’s illegal to buy, sell, kill or capture any wild animal or trade its parts without a licence. Nepal is a signatory to the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES), which bans trade of wildlife products without a permit.

countryFacts.payments.text: The economy is largely cash-based; however, credit cards can be used in major stores, hotels and restaurants. ATMs are available in larger cities such as Kathmandu and Pokhara.
ATMs are not reliable outside main tourist sites.
particularly in remote areas, where ATMs may not be available and credit cards not accepted.

countryFacts.safety.text: There’s a low rate of serious crime in Nepal but take precautions.
Watch out for pickpockets and bag-snatchers
Political protests, demonstrations and strikes are fairly common in Nepal.
On 26 August 2026, major flooding in Rasuwa district and the Nepal-China border area caused widespread damage.
The authorities have warned of the risk of further flooding.

countryFacts.bestTimeToVisit.text: Travel during the monsoon season (normally June to October) can be hazardous. Flooding and landslides can lead to impassable roads, delays to journeys, or cut off towns and villages for days at a time.
